findings.detail: The constructor's struct-literal body currently assigns `post_ready_route: SubtitlePostReadyRoute::LegacySubtitleReviewV1`; this line must be deleted as a logically necessary consequence of removing the field. The task card should say the constructor's signature and its three preserved-field assignments stay unchanged, not that the constructor body is untouched.

At closure, check whether any doc/ledger prose still describes SubtitlePostReadyRoute/post_ready_route/new_s150_localization as current behavior and flag it stale; the edit itself may be out of this task's code scope.

SubtitleJob has no #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], so already-queued job JSON containing a stray legacy post_ready_route key will still deserialize successfully post-removal (ignored). The test that implicitly covered this (legacy_subtitle_job_json_defaults_to_legacy_route) is being deleted; consider keeping a slimmed variant that decodes legacy JSON with a stray post_ready_route key and asserts the result matches SubtitleJob::new(..), since this is a queued-job payload shape, not just an internal API.

Removing post_ready_route changes SubtitleJob's derived PartialEq/Eq semantics: two jobs formerly distinguished by route become equal whenever asset/project/target_language match. Nothing shown relies on route-based inequality, but note the behavior change in the closure record.
